claims.claim: Severian of Gabala was the bishop of Gabala in Syria, active in the late fourth and early fifth centuries (c. 355–408/425).
He was a popular preacher in Constantinople around 400–404 and became the chief opponent of Patriarch John Chrysostom.
The work titled *Fragmenta in epistulam i ad Timotheum* consists of excerpts from Severian’s commentary on the First Epistle to Timothy that are preserved in catena collections.
The fragments are found in a Vatican Greek manuscript (Vat. gr. 2217) catalogued by the Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana.
